shorts.hook: Lake Vostok was sealed under Antarctica's ice for millions of years.
shorts.title: Lake Vostok's Water Rushed Up the Drill Hole, Then Froze
shorts.outro: What happens next is even worse. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: When a Russian drill broke into Lake Vostok in 2012, sealed under nearly 3,800 meters of Antarctic ice for millions of years, the lake water surged up the borehole on its own and froze inside it.

shorts.hook: Scientists drilled through Antarctic ice and hit a rock that was alive.
shorts.title: Nobody Knows What These Sponges Under Antarctica Are Eating
shorts.outro: And it only gets deeper from here. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: A borehole through an Antarctic ice shelf hit a boulder covered in sponges living in total darkness, hundreds of kilometers from the nearest sunlit water, and scientists still don't know what they eat.

shorts.hook: Scientists melted a hole through 740 meters of Antarctic ice.
shorts.title: Fish Swam Up to a Camera 740 Meters Under Antarctic Ice
shorts.outro: Then the ice above them started to move. The full dive is linked below.
shorts.description: In 2015 scientists melted a hole through about 740 meters of Antarctic ice, dropped a camera into a 10-meter gap of dark, freezing seawater, and pale see-through fish came right up to the lens.
